articles.title: Falcons Draft 2027: Way-Too-Early 2027 NFL Mock Draft 1.0
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out fo...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out for the first game against the Pittsburgh Steelers . But that's not why we're here. Draft season is year-round nowadays, and the Falcons need multiple players throughout the roster if they're going to build a sturdy foundation to start competing for the division/conference sooner rather than later. Atlanta has done a great job not overextending in the short term, owning the most cap space in 2027, despite extending Drake London , Bijan Robinson , Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron this offseason. However, even with the potential depth that money can bring, general manager Ian Cunningham and President Matt Ryan have to hit on the draft. So, we're going to get a jump on next year's draft by pinpointing seven picks in this way-too-early 2027 NFL mock draft.

Round 1, Pick 6: Darian Mensah, QB, Miami

I'm buying into the hype early. The former Duke transfer has come out of the gate firing, albeit against Stanford and Florida A&M. Mensah's 91.1% completion percentage is the second-best start to a college football season for any quarterback with 40+ attempts in the first two games, while his 271.7 Passer Efficiency Rating is the best. 41-of-45 for 653 yards, eight touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Miami is looking to run through the ACC with ease, and hopefully, that means we see plenty of NFL-caliber throws from Mensah that will make him the next transfer quarterback who impresses scouts this season.

Round 2, Pick 38: Samson Okunlola, OT, Miami

To build the future, you have to fortify the foundation, and that means Atlanta has to acquire a left tackle, so Jake Matthews can be the family man he deserves to be. Samson Okunlola's movement skills, especially his absurdly quick feet, are just one of his impressive traits that scouts will bet on if he comes out after this season. Okunlola's 6'6", 330-pound frame gives him such impressive size and he has experience playing inside as well.

Round 3, Pick 70: Tavion Gadson, DT, Kentucky

With Brandon Dorlus heading to the edge, the Falcons lose the interior pressure that Dorlus and, to a lesser extent, Ruke Orhorhoro brought on opposing quarterbacks. Tavion Gadson immediately brings that pass-rush juice back to the Falcons' line along with a knack for using his athleticism and size (6'4", 302 pounds) to stuff up the A-gaps.

Round 4, Pick 105: Niki Prongos, OT, Stanford

I couldn't help myself, and if Cunningham and Stefanski were met with the same choice, I don't think they would help themselves either. Niki Prongos hadn't started playing football until his senior year of high school, choosing to play baseball and basketball instead. Even in high school, he played tight end and defensive tackle alongside his duties at tackle. Prongos is such a fun athlete and would be a stellar pickup for Bill Callahan.

Round 5, Pick 179: Bruce Mitchell, C, BYU

#63 in white and blue has a case to be the best center in college football, and it would not surprise me if he finds a way into day two when it's all said and done. Mitchell has a stout anchor in pass protection alongside some strong hands in the run game. With this move, the Falcons would solve all three of their "problems" along the offensive line in one draft.

Round 6, Pick 216: Fluff Bothwell, RB, Mississippi State

Brian Robinson Jr. feels like a rental for this season, but the future of backing up Bijan Robinson can look like a running back like Fluff Bothwell. Don't let the name fool you; there is absolutely nothing soft about his game. Bothwell is 5'10", 230 pounds and, for a man of that size, he has impressive agility.

Round 7, Pick 220: Duce Robinson, WR, Florida State

KJ Duff is one of those players in the 2027 draft you wish had transferred to another team so he could get more eyes on his performance with a quarterback who can get him the ball. The same goes for Florida State receiver Duce Robinson. Robinson is 6'6", 230 pounds and has an incredibly large catch radius, while allowing Drake London to work more in the slot and Kyle Pitts over the middle of the field.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Said Seahawks 'Cannot F--k With' Patriots WRs in Trending Sideline Video from Week 1
articles.summary: A.J. Brown was confident in the ability of the New England Patriots' receivers to beat the Seattle Seahawks' secondary in New England's 13-10 loss to Seattle on Wednesday.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown was confident in the ability of the New England Patriots' receivers to beat the Seattle Seahawks' secondary in New England's 13-10 loss to Seattle on Wednesday.

"If y'all boys just could hold up, we gonna score this s--t," Brown told the Patriots' offensive linemen during the game in a video released by the team. "They cannot f--k with none of us at wide receiver, I'm telling you. We running wide open, you hear me?"

Brown caught three of his four targets for 26 yards against the Seahawks before exiting the game in the third quarter due to an ankle injury .

New England eventually placed him on injured reserve Friday, meaning that he'll miss at least four games before he can return.

On the same drive that Brown suffered the injury against Seattle, the Patriots kicked a field goal to take a 10-0 lead in the Super Bowl LX rematch.

While the Seahawks were without starting quarterback Sam Darnold since their opening drive of the game due to a hip injury , they were able to swing momentum in their favor throughout the rest of the game.

Seattle scored 13 consecutive points to jump in front, as New England's offense struggled without Brown.

The four Patriots drives after his injury ended with a punt and three interceptions by quarterback Drake Maye. His final interception came with New England in field-goal range as just under 30 seconds remained in the fourth quarter, sealing the final result.

Maye was sacked three times in the game after he was sacked on six occasions during the Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks last season.

Outside of Brown, Mack Hollins was the only New England wide receiver to surpass 20 yards in Wednesday's defeat.

articles.title: Travis Kelce made unusual $35,000 decision as Eighty-Seven and Running faced questions over its operations
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s latest charitable decision has drawn attention for a reason that goes beyond the money involved. In January 2026, the Kansas City Chief.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s latest charitable decision has drawn attention for a reason that goes beyond the money involved. In January 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs star chose not to send his latest $35,000 charity prize to his own foundation. Instead, he directed it to a Kansas City nonprofit he has supported for years, a move that comes as questions surround the governance and financial reporting of his organization.Travis Kelce sends $35,000 prize to established Kansas City nonprofitKelce earned the money after winning the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Charity Challenge for the third time on January 7, 2026. Unlike his previous victories in 2020 and 2024, however, the prize will not benefit his Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation.The funds are going to Operation Breakthrough, a long-standing Kansas City organization that works with children, teenagers and families. Kelce has previously supported the nonprofit through his foundation’s partnership with its Ignition Lab, a program focused on workforce development for teens.The choice also comes shortly after Taylor Swift donated $250,000 to Operation Breakthrough, adding another high-profile connection to the organization.Kelce’s decision stands out because it breaks from his own recent pattern. Rather than keeping the award money within a foundation he established, he opted for an organization with an established structure and track record.CharityWatch CEO and executive director Laurie Styron viewed that decision positively.“As for Kelce’s decision to donate his contest winnings to an established charity, in the short term this was the right call,” said CharityWatch CEO and executive director Laurie Styron in her interview with The Arizona Republic. “The people operating the foundation need time to get their accounting, governance, and legal house in order. It was the responsible move under the circumstances.”Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation faces questions over its operationsThe timing of Kelce’s decision is important. His Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation, which he launched in 2015, has come under scrutiny following a review of its federal tax filings by The Arizona Republic.The reporting raised questions about the foundation’s spending and internal structure. Over a three-year period, the organization reportedly spent about 41 cents of every dollar on charitable activities. It also paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to A&A Management Group, a company co-founded by Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes.The foundation has also reportedly operated with only two board members and without several standard officer positions, including a president and secretary.Styron raised concerns about the relationship between the charity and the management company.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” Styron said after reviewing the filings. “That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”The foundation has disputed the implication that its spending figures tell the full story. Aaron Eanes, its executive director, said expenses connected to charitable work had been incorrectly classified as management costs on IRS filings for nearly a decade.According to Eanes, the organization has been correcting those filings. He also said management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025, while plans are underway to expand the board and strengthen reporting.He stated that the organization is “dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards,” according to The Arizona Republic.Kelce’s move therefore carries significance beyond one $35,000 award. It highlights how athlete-led charities can face intense scrutiny once their public profile grows, and why financial transparency and independent oversight matter just as much as charitable intentions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Jackson has been "reluctant" to negotiate a long-term extension "for whatever reason" despite the Ravens being willing to make him the highest-paid quarterback in the NFL, per Schefter .

Jackson is currently under contract through 2027.

However, it's understandable that the Ravens may be motivated to finalize a new deal at the end of this year in order to avoid his $84.3 million cap hit during the 2027 season (via Spotrac ).

Schefter also reported Saturday that "no deal is expected anytime soon," though.

Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta previously said that he was "optimistic" about reaching a contract extension agreement with Jackson on Sept. 2, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Despite the lack of an extension, a change of scenery for the two-time MVP doesn't appear to be on the horizon.

On Saturday, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported that the relationship between Jackson and the Ravens is the "healthiest it's been" while both sides have "every intention of continuing their work together for years to come."

Jackson has spent all eight seasons of his career in Baltimore, establishing himself as one of the league's top quarterbacks.

While injuries limited him to 13 games in 2025, he still completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 2,549 yards and 21 touchdowns compared to seven interceptions. He also rushed for 349 yards and two scores.

articles.title: Inspiring story on balancing motherhood and career:“You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to”-How Brittany Mahomes continues to inspire her children

articles.body: For Brittany Mahomes, motherhood did not mean putting her own ambitions on hold. Instead, becoming a mother of three appears to have changed the way she approaches both family and work. The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes says her children have given her a stronger sense of purpose, while also pushing her to show them what it means to dream big and work hard.How motherhood changed Brittany Mahomes’ outlook on lifeBrittany Mahomes entered motherhood while already building a life of her own. She had a background in soccer, fitness and business, while her relationship with Patrick Mahomes placed her close to the intense world of professional football.Then came a new role that changed everything.Brittany and Patrick welcomed their first child, daughter Sterling, in 2021. Their family grew again with the arrival of son Bronze in 2022 and daughter Golden in 2025.Three children later, Brittany says motherhood has changed more than her daily routine. It has influenced the way she thinks about her goals, her time and the example she wants to set at home.“Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,” Brittany, 30, told Yahoo Entertainment in June 2026. “It really reshaped and redefined a lot of things in my life.”That change does not sound like a retreat from ambition. If anything, Brittany appears to have found another reason to keep moving.She explained that motherhood has made her more deliberate about the opportunities she takes and the people and causes she gives her attention to. Her priorities have become clearer, with family now playing a major role in how she measures what is worth pursuing.That shift is especially meaningful for someone whose life has long been lived in the public eye.Brittany Mahomes wants her children to dream without limitsOne of the strongest themes in Brittany’s recent comments is the importance of showing her children that their dreams should not come with unnecessary limits.“It’s made me more intentional, more purposeful and, honestly, more motivated to keep going and keep showing my kids that there are no boundaries in front of you. You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to. You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard and do the hard things to do the fun things.”There is a simple lesson behind those words. Brittany does not want her children to learn about ambition only through their father’s NFL career. She wants them to see it through her actions, too.That means continuing to build her own professional identity while raising three young children.For Brittany, success is not just about having a busy schedule or being attached to a famous sports family. It is about demonstrating that family and personal ambition can exist at the same time.That message becomes even more powerful because her children are growing up around two parents with demanding careers.Brittany Mahomes wants her children to see both parents work hardPatrick Mahomes has spent much of his adult life under the brightest lights in American sports. His NFL career demands long hours, travel, preparation and an enormous physical commitment.Brittany understands that her children see that effort.But she also wants them to see hers.“At the end of the day, my kids are watching me, and I want them to know that I’m working hard,” she told Yahoo!Life in February 2024. “I’m out here doing things as well, because they noticed their dad’s gone all the time. And he’s working hard and doing stuff that he loves. So, I want them to see both of us going out and conquering the world.”That perspective gives her story a more personal edge. Brittany is not simply trying to fit a career around motherhood. She is thinking about what her children will learn by watching her navigate both.Her message is also about balance. Children may see the finished result of a parent’s work, but they rarely see everything that happens before it.Brittany wants her children to understand that achievement requires effort, patience and a willingness to take on difficult moments.Brittany Mahomes is learning when to say noMotherhood has also changed the way Brittany views her time.“I think when you become a mom, you learn to say no to things that aren’t as important and focus on what’s best for your life and your family,” she said.It is a particularly relatable part of her story.A larger career can bring more invitations, projects and opportunities. Yet having children can force a person to decide which ones truly matter.For Brittany, that appears to have created a clearer filter. Instead of trying to do everything, she wants to focus on things that align with her values and the example she hopes to give her children.That does not mean ambition has disappeared. It means the definition of ambition has changed.Her goals now sit alongside school days, family moments, parenting responsibilities and the realities of raising three children while living under constant public attention.Brittany Mahomes is building a legacy beyond Patrick MahomesBrittany will always be closely connected to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Their marriage, family and shared life have naturally made them one of the NFL’s most recognizable couples.Yet her story has increasingly moved beyond that connection.Her soccer background helped shape her interest in sports. Her fitness work gave her an independent professional identity. Her involvement in women’s soccer has also allowed her to participate in the growth of the sport from a different side of the field.Now, motherhood has added another layer to that journey.Rather than viewing her role as a choice between being a mother and pursuing her own goals, Brittany appears determined to show her children that both can have a place in the same life.Her approach is not about pretending that balancing everything is easy. It is about understanding what deserves her energy.And perhaps that is the most inspiring part of her story.Brittany Mahomes is not telling her children to dream big simply because she wants them to succeed. She is trying to show them what that looks like by continuing to dream, work and build while being present for the family she has created.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Rumors Update Parker Washington, Jaguars Contract Buzz After Michael Wilson, Cardinals Deal
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington is reportedly on track to start the 2026 season on an expiring contract.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington is reportedly on track to start the 2026 season on an expiring contract.

NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported Saturday it is "unlikely" Washington will sign an extension before the Jaguars open the season Sunday afternoon.

According to Wolfe, the Jaguars previously "explored" a deal in the range of the three-year, $75 million extension Michael Wilson recently signed with the Arizona Cardinals.

Wilson signed his deal, which included $47 million in guaranteed money, after topping 1,000 receiving yards in 17 games of his third season with the Cardinals.

Washington is currently heading into the 2026 season under a $3.7 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie deal .

He told reporters that as of Thursday he was still getting daily updates from his agent about ongoing communication with the Jaguars.

The Jaguars wide receiver also said he felt his job was "to come out here and stay ready to go and just do my job."

Washington recorded 847 receiving yards in 16 games during his own third NFL season.

Most of his production came down the stretch of the campaign. He made 22 catches on 32 targets for 400 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the final four games of the Jags' push for the playoffs.

Washington was rewarded in the Wild Card round with a team-high 12 targets, of which he caught seven for 107 receiving yards and a touchdown before the Jaguars were eliminated by the Buffalo Bills.

ESPN's Michael DiRocco reported last month that Washington had earned his spot as the Jaguars' WR1 after working as Trevor Lawrence's "favorite target" in training camp.

Regardless of the wide receiver's contract status, the Jaguars will hope Lawrence and Washington are able to continue building on that connection when kicking off the season Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the visiting Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: San Diego State's offense can't match defense's performance in loss to UCLA
articles.summary: Despite the defense largely holding UCLA’s offense in check, SDSU’s offense managed just 189 yards and one touchdown in a 28-10 loss.
articles.body:
PASADENA -- San Diego State 's defense did practically everything they could to keep the Aztecs in the game against UCLA . They just needed the offense to come along for the ride.

Despite the defense largely holding UCLA's offense in check, SDSU's offense managed just 189 yards and one touchdown — coming effectively in garbage time — in a 28-10 loss to the Bruins at the Rose Bowl on Saturday.

"Inefficiency on offense led to a bunch of snaps for the defense," head coach Sean Lewis said. "Starting three and out there constantly, we were behind in the field position game. So I think just the culmination of snaps, the inefficiency on offense. It starts with the play calling, with myself, the leadership throughout the course of the week, so that we can have more success and flip the field."

Nowhere was SDSU's offensive struggle more apparent than in the passing game. The Aztecs completed just six passes for 45 yards, and several deep shots by quarterback Jayden Denegal were wildly off-target.

"[We] felt like we had good matchups on the edge," Lewis said. "There was a lot of single-high coverage. Again, those are good, calculated shots downrange. We got balls on hands that we didn't catch. We had other guys wide open that we missed."

San Diego State held up defensively for the majority of the game. They kept UCLA scoreless in the first half and limited them to just seven points through three quarters.

"I think we did a good job with our aggression," said sophomore cornerback Mike Lindsay, who intercepted UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava in the second quarter. "I think that caught them by surprise. I think that they're thinking we were going to be a little bit weaker than how we came out there, and we did a good job stopping the run and containing [Iamaleava] because he likes his ground, he likes to run around, but we kept him in the pocket [and] kept him on the ground."

Despite the defense's containment of UCLA's offense, SDSU's own unit generated even less. They failed to score in the first three quarters and managed their only touchdown with 2:28 remaining in the fourth.

"We knew how to scheme up and get our guys in the right spot," sophomore offensive lineman Michael Watkins said. "I think it was just blocking in the moment. You know, it was just the little letups … it would be [blowing off] technique and it would let up."

Eventually, the defense collapsed under the weight of the pressure. As Lewis noted, having the defense on the field for as long as they were led to exhaustion. UCLA won the time-of-possession battle by nearly 10 minutes, and SDSU ran out of gas, allowing three rushing touchdowns in the fourth quarter for a final result that was closer than the score indicated.

"Good teams are able to play balanced and use special teams as a weapon to flip the field," Lewis said. "So when you got two out of three phases doing well, you've got to evaluate and assess what's going on with that other phase as you go forward with it."

The Aztecs' next attempt to produce a more balanced performance will take place at home, against James Madison at 7 p.m. on Sept. 19. Despite Saturday's difficult results, Watkins expressed optimism that his group is capable of a stronger outcome.

"We just know what we can do, and we know we can keep punching them in the mouth, and we know how it feels like," he said. "You know, we [weren't] finishing, we [weren't] getting the end zone, but the way we [were] coming off the field, it felt like we're [really] close. We just gotta get it in."

articles.summary: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — A missed extra point was the difference between #3 O’Gorman and #5 Harrisburg in the 48th annual Bob Burns Dakota Bowl, and this y...
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — A missed extra point was the difference between #3 O'Gorman and #5 Harrisburg in the 48th annual Bob Burns Dakota Bowl, and this year the visiting Tigers will head back home with the win, 21-20.

O'Gorman scored on their first drive of the ballgame, a long sustained push capped off with a short rushing touchdown, but from there the offense went stagnant the rest of the first half.

Harrisburg had a nice, long drive of their own capped off with a QB sneak from Jonah Young to tie things up, a pick six for Bryson Esser gave the Tigers a lead heading into the locker room as well.

Out of the break, O'Gorman's offense re-found its rhythm and capped a six minute drive with a Brady Majeres rushing touchdown to tie the game at 14.

Harrisburg would march down and score to retake a touchdown lead, but the Knights responded this time, hitting paydirt for the six, unfortunately for them, a strong Harrisburg push on the line caused enough pressure to force a miss and the Tigers led by one, 21-20.

The Knights had a chance in the final minute as they got the ball with 53 seconds left, but an untimely fumble, recovered by Harrisburg marked the end of the game.

O'Gorman moves to 1-2 after the loss while Harrisburg is 2-1.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Predicted to Pair With $29 Million WR Star in NFL Draft
articles.summary: Ohio State superstar WR projected to land in NFC East. The post Jeremiah Smith Predicted to Pair With $29 Million WR Star in NFL Draft appeared first on HEAV...
articles.body:
The New York Giants may already have Malik Nabers returning to their offense, but one 2027 NFL mock draft has them adding an even bigger prize alongside him.

Athlon Sports' Luke Easterling projected the Giants to select Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith with the No. 3 overall pick in his updated mock draft after Week 1 of the college football season.

For Jaxson Dart , it would potentially give him one of the NFL's most dangerous young receiving duos.

Giants Predicted to Draft Jeremiah Smith No. 3

"It looks like Malik Nabers is on track to return in Week 1 after missing most of last season with a knee injury, but even with him at full strength and the addition of third-rounder Malachi Fields , the Giants would still be wise not to pass on the chance to land Smith," Easterling wrote.

"The best overall player in this entire class, Smith is one of the best receiver prospects I've ever evaluated, and would instantly make this one of the most talented pass-catching groups in the NFL."

That is a massive statement considering the talent expected to be available in the 2027 draft.

Easterling still has Smith going behind Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore . If New York were sitting at No. 3, though, he believes the Giants should take the best overall player rather than force another position.

The Ohio State star entered his junior season with 163 catches for 2,558 yards and 27 touchdowns over his first two years. He then opened 2026 with eight catches for 151 yards and two touchdowns in a 56-3 win over Ball State.

That moved him to 171 career receptions, 2,709 yards and 29 touchdowns after only one game of his junior season.

Jeremiah Smith Could Give Jaxson Dart Elite Giants Duo

The Giants selected Nabers No. 6 overall in 2024 and signed him to a four-year, $29.2 million fully guaranteed rookie contract.

He immediately looked like a franchise receiver, catching 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie. His second season ended after only four games when he suffered a torn ACL.

Nabers practiced fully throughout this week but was listed as questionable for Sunday's opener against the Dallas Cowboys .

Pairing him with Smith would give Dart two young receivers who were each viewed as elite prospects before reaching the NFL.

"Giving a young quarterback like Jaxson Dart a trio like that would be a massive win for the Giants' future," Easterling wrote, also including Fields in the group.

Dart gave New York reasons to keep building around him during his rookie year.

The 2025 first-round pick started 12 games and completed 63.7% of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions. He added 487 rushing yards and nine scores, giving him 24 total touchdowns.

His biggest limitation was that he barely got to play with Nabers, who appeared in only four games before the knee injury ended his season.

New York spent the offseason adding help, including Fields in the third round, but Easterling doesn't believe that should stop the Giants from taking Smith if the opportunity comes.

It's far too early to know whether New York will actually pick anywhere near No. 3.

But if the Giants do land that high in the 2027 draft, Easterling's prediction would put arguably the class' best overall player opposite their $29 million star and give Dart an entirely different level of firepower.

Speaking ahead of the game, he acknowledged the quality of Houston's defense and the difficulty of playing the Texans at home."Yeah, I mean, it's getting a chance to go play football against a really, really good team," Allen said. "A team that was obviously in the playoffs last year. We understand what their defense is and has been. They have a fantastic coach over there. Those guys are gonna be ready to play."This time, Buffalo enters the matchup with plenty of offensive firepower. James Cook is coming off a league-leading 1,621 rushing yards in 2025, while the Bills also added DJ Moore to their receiving group.For Allen, though, the mission is straightforward. articles.title: After 18 years in Baltimore, John Harbaugh faces his biggest challenge yet: Turning around the New York Giants
articles.summary: The start of the new NFL season always brings a few things that take getting used to. Perhaps one of the most head-turning sights will be walking the sidelines of MetLife Stadium during the final game on Sunday.
articles.body: The start of the new NFL season always brings a few things that take getting used to. Perhaps one of the most head-turning sights will be walking the sidelines of MetLife Stadium during the final game on Sunday. John Harbaugh will be making his regular-season debut with the New York Giants that night in New Jersey in a divisional matchup vs. the Dallas Cowboys that could set the tone for both teams’ seasons. It’s bound to be a disarming sight: For the first time in 18 years, Harbaugh won’t be in the black-and-purple of the Baltimore Ravens. It’ll be a new home stadium, new colors, a bunch of new players and new assistants around Harbaugh after nearly two decades in Charm City. But some things will be the same. From what his players have said ahead of the season, expect the Giants to be physical and – even after a last-place 4-13 record last year and a string of disappointing campaigns – winning remains the standard. “How do you go out there and compete at this level if you don’t expect to win? If you don’t expect to win, you certainly aren’t going to,” Harbaugh said earlier this month. “I’ve said this before: we expect and we plan to and we’ll be playing to win every single one of our games this year. That’s our expectation, that’s our plan, that’s what we’ll be striving for. We think we can, we believe we can wholeheartedly.” That will be music to the ears of Giants fans who have had to endure a depressing decade, with just one winning season since 2016. A string of six coaches in that time span, including interims, has turned the Meadowlands into a football no-man’s land following a period of success that included two Super Bowl championships and frequent trips to the playoffs. Consistency and winning are Harbaugh’s bread and butter. His run in Baltimore included 12 trips to the playoffs, one Super Bowl championship and a 180-113 record in 18 seasons. He had fewer losing seasons in those 18 years (three) than the Giants have had this decade (five). Those Ravens teams were shaped in the tried-and-true image of the Harbaugh family: Tough defense, strong running games and superstar quarterbacks under center. It’s a recipe that Giants fans are familiar with and one they might be able to run back this season under new leadership. “The principles of the vision you’re talking about, that’s that word, are written in stone, and they’re football principles,” Harbaugh said at his opening press conference earlier this year. “They’re self-evident truths. They aren’t ever going to change. Those are things you carry with you through 18 years or 42 years or whatever it is. You carry those principles with you. You learn what they are, and they’re just non-compromised. They can’t be. They have to happen.” One of those ingredients appears to already be present in northern New Jersey in second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart. Drafted out of Ole Miss to be the future star under center for the Giants, Dart looked promising in his rookie year even after missing two games with a concussion. The expectations for him were high even before Harbaugh became his new head coach after a relatively quick search following Harbaugh and the Ravens’ split in January – a search that even included the President of the United States pressing the Giants to hire Harbaugh. So far, Dart’s connection with Harbaugh seems strong, with the quarterback describing his leader as intense and in love with the game of football. Oh, and Dart loves that Harbaugh has something to prove after the Ravens let him go. “He’s got a chip on his shoulder. I’m interested to see how his demeanor continues to grow as we go forward,” he said. So far, that chip has manifested in ramping up the intensity for the Giants. In training camp, that meant frequent practices in pads and a style seen more often in the college game than in the pros. Isaiah Likely, a tight end who followed Harbaugh to the Giants from Baltimore, said it all felt normal to him, though it was clearly different for some of his teammates. “I feel like that’s normal to me. Like, I’m just – if I wake up, I’m putting on cleats. That’s just the mantra I have,” he told reporters last week. “So, hearing how Giants training camp was in the past, that was kind of mind-boggling to me, but I feel like the guys embraced it. We had a good time in Greenbrier (the West Virginia resort where training camp opened) and then when we got here, I feel like now everybody’s on the same mantra: If we’re in the building, it’s all ball.” “I see why his teams are always physical,” added cornerback Greg Newsome II. “His teams are always smart. They’re not penalized much, and everyone’s pretty disciplined. I think that’s a credit to what he does as a coach and just being a part of it this little time I’ve been here so far, I can tell why in late December and January, they’re playing meaningful games every single year.” Harbaugh’s influence on the organization has already stretched beyond the field and into the front office. Giants general manager Joe Schoen, who is entering his fifth season as general manager of the Giants and was feeling the heat last season as his team floundered, has been seeking his head coach’s counsel on personnel matters frequently in the offseason. “He’s immersed in the personnel, and he’s helpful, makes us think outside the box, challenges us. And that’s what has ultimately led to a lot of good conversations, communications, ultimately making the best decision for the New York Giants,” Schoen said.

articles.title: How Travis Kelce turned a $3.13M rookie contract into investments in Tequila, Pancake Mix, and a Theme Park
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce signed his first NFL contract in 2013 for $3.13 million over four years. That number feels almost quaint now. Thirteen years later, the K.
articles.body: Travis Kelce signed his first NFL contract in 2013 for $3.13 million over four years. That number feels almost quaint now. Thirteen years later, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end has built a portfolio that stretches from canned tequila to Formula 1, from a light beer company to a nationwide car wash chain. His $90 million net worth in 2026, per Celebrity Net Worth, is only partly explained by football. The rest is a story about a player who treated every offseason like a second career.What businesses does Travis Kelce actually own?The list is genuinely eclectic, and that's the point. Travis Kelce has never chased one industry. He co-owns Garage Beer with brother Jason, becoming the company's largest investors in June 2024. "It was just an opportunity to be part of a brand that I really enjoy," Kelce told Forbes at the time. CEO Andy Sauer confirmed the brothers have "by far" the biggest ownership stake in the company.Before Garage Beer, there was Casa Azul Tequila Soda in 2023, a canned cocktail brand built on real tequila rather than malt liquor. Kelce took an equity stake ahead of Super Bowl LVII and became its ambassador. "Not only do I know how to get wins on the board, I also like to make sure everyone is having a good time anywhere I go," he said in the brand's announcement.Then there's Kodiak Cakes, the high-protein, whole-grain pancake company. Kelce joined a star-studded athlete group led by Patricof Co. back in 2022. "I've been a fan of Kodiak products for a long time and excited to officially collaborate with the brand," he said. It's the kind of investment that aligns with his training, but also quietly bets on the health food market's growth.How did Travis Kelce end up investing in Six Flags?This one has an origin story worth telling. Kelce grew up in northeast Ohio, where family trips to Cedar Point were a fixture. That nostalgia factor played into his October 2025 decision to partner with activist hedge fund Jana Partners to take a stake in Six Flags Entertainment. The group, which also includes former Gap CEO Glenn Murphy, now holds approximately 9% of Six Flags. By 2026, Kelce had been named the brand's official ambassador.The move is less celebrity publicity stunt and more activist play. Jana Partners specifically targets companies it believes are underperforming and pushes for operational improvements. Kelce joining that group as a major investor signals he's not just signing on for social media posts.What is Travis Kelce's biggest off-field investment?The Alpine F1 deal stands apart from everything else. In October 2023, Kelce joined an Otro Capital-led consortium alongside Patrick Mahomes, Rory McIlroy, Anthony Joshua, and Trent Alexander-Arnold in a $210 million investment round into the Renault-backed Alpine Formula One team. Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney were already in through their Maximum Effort Investments group."I am thrilled to lead an investor group and join forces with Patrick and the team at Otro Capital on this exciting venture with Alpine F1," Kelce said in the official announcement. "Our shared passion for excellence and innovation forms the cornerstone of this partnership." The deal pushed Alpine's total valuation past $1 billion.How does Travis Kelce's business strategy actually work?What ties all of this together is a pattern that's easy to miss if you're only looking at the brand names. Kelce invests in things he already uses or genuinely cares about. He grew up near Cedar Point. He drinks light beer. He's a serious athlete who pays attention to what he eats. None of these feel like a financial advisor's cold pitch.His endorsement income has grown to over $30 million annually according to sports marketing analyst Bob Dorfman, nearly double his $17 million NFL salary. That figure didn't materialize overnight. It built through consistent visibility, three Super Bowl rings, and a public profile that expanded dramatically after his relationship with Taylor Swift began in 2023.The $100 million podcast deal with Amazon's Wondery, confirmed by Variety, CNN, and ESPN, is the clearest signal of what Kelce and his brother Jason built independent of football. The podcast ranked as the fourth biggest in the United States across all platforms in Q1 2024. His career NFL earnings now sit above $111 million, per Celebrity Net Worth, with a new three-year Chiefs extension worth up to $57.7 million signed in March 2026.From a $3.13 million rookie deal to a nine-figure podcast, a Formula 1 team, and a 9% stake in an American theme park empire, Kelce has done something most athletes never manage. He kept building after the game clock stopped.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 3 Big Factors in the Buccaneers' Week 1 Showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals
articles.summary: Tampa Bay will kick off the season with hopes of a division title when they face Cincy on Sunday
articles.body:
Tampa Bay will kick off the season with hopes of a division title when they face Cincy on Sunday

It all starts again for the NFL; the first Sunday of the regular season is upon us. That means it's time for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to get back to business.

The Bucs finished the 2025 NFL regular season at 8-9, which tied them at the top of the NFC South, but they failed to qualify for the playoffs due to tiebreakers. They will enter the new campaign with a fully-charged Baker Mayfield at the helm, and an eye on returning to the postseason.

Their Week 1 opponents, the Cincinnati Bengals , have been one of the strangest franchises in recent memory, and perhaps ever in the history of the National Football League. Despite having superstar-caliber quarterback Joe Burrow and wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase, the team isn't considered a true postseason threat. They could win the division and still be an afterthought in terms of true, Super Bowl contenders.

But the pieces are in place for the team to have a successful season, and that starts with Cincy. There are a few factors that could decide whether or not the Tampa team will come out on top this week.

Baker Mayfield has been a football folk hero for years, due to his late-game heroics, emotional play, and outstanding ability. The Buccaneers will only go as far as their undisputed leader can take them, and he has the opportunity to prove that he's truly among the elite in 2026.

For Tampa to return to the Playoffs, Mayfield must limit his mistakes. Even in his normal comfort zone, he has forced plays at times, sometimes relying on his arm and instincts when it would be better to live and fight another day. However, he's also limited those kinds of errors in recent years.

Since coming to Tampa, Mayfield has posted a 95-to-37 touchdown-to-interception ratio over the past three seasons, averaging 2.57 scores for every pick. That kind of output against the Bengals would likely get the year started off with a victory, while also setting a promising pace for the rest of the regular season.

With fellow wide receiver Jalen McMillan ruled out for the week, the former third-round pick can fill the 'gimmick' role, or the 'X' position, in the wideout corps. He'll likely line up in unique spots and do a lot of different things to stay involved on the offense on Sunday. For the Bucs to find success, he will need to make plays when given the opportunity - particularly on third down.

Johnson, the adopted brother of Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix , has been a bit under the radar in terms of his playmaking ability. He had 28 catches for 322 yards and five TDs in his rookie campaign a season ago. A breakout performance could provide momentum the receiver can carry all through the year.

Last year, Tampa Bay's defense was fairly middle-of-the-pack overall, with one major strength and one major weakness. They were excellent against the run but vulnerable through the air, something they will look to remedy by kickoff.

They suffered a big loss with the retirement of LaVonte David , the 14-year Bucs veteran who provided hard hits and tough love as the team's captain. He's on his way to Canton someday, but in the meantime, the team has made some additions to shore up their pass rush.

Perhaps the player to focus on this week will be newcomer Al-Quadin Muhammad . The outside linebacker had 11 sacks a year ago for the Detroit Lions , despite not starting a single game. He could provide the pressure that buries Burrow and the Bengals in this season's opener.

articles.title: Jason Chaffetz: 4 ways to make football more exciting to watch
articles.summary: Former Rep. Jason Chaffetz argues the NFL kicking game has become too predictable and lays out four ways the league could make field goals, extra points and kickoffs more exciting.
articles.body: It’s time to "fix the kick" in the NFL. With the Chief’s Harrison Butker’s 69-yard field goal in the pre-season, it was demonstrated yet again that today’s kickers are better than ever. Year after year they kick it higher, further, and straighter. Usually, the placekicker is the leading scorer on the team, but nobody cares because the kicking game has become boring and predictable. The NFL failed to make it more interesting when they moved back extra points and changed kickoffs. Here are four ways to boot it up a big notch: CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE 1. Put a crossbar on the top of the field goal posts Make it a rectangle that challenges the placekicker to "place" it in the uprights, without kicking it too high, where the referee has to make a judgment call about whether the kick was between the posts. This will make every kick more interesting. 38-yard kicks are too routine. Extra points are so boring it’s time to go get a snack. All NFL level kickers can hit 70–80-yard field goals in practice. More and more coaches are taking chances that their guy can hit it from more than 50 yards out. The primary difference between high school, college, and pro kicking is distance with trajectory. Lining up approximately 7.5 yards behind the line of scrimmage, the defense surges so they are usually about 5 yards from the kick coming off the ground. The pros need to get the ball at least 11 feet in the air to avoid it being blocked. It’s hard to do, but they all do it with relative ease. Time to make it more difficult. Let’s change the "field goal" to an actual goal. Similar to golf, kickers use their 9-iron on all kicks. They are only challenged to hit it long and straight. Kicking it into the target is much different, more challenging, and will be more exciting to watch. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! 2. articles.title: Former Texas A&M coach Klint Kubiak set for NFL HC debut
articles.summary: Klint Kubiak began his coaching career in Aggieland and will lead the Las Vegas Raiders against Miami in his NFL head-coaching debut.
articles.body:
There will be another Texas A&M alum beginning the 2026 NFL regular season as a head coach . Klint Kubiak will make his head-coaching debut with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, 16 years after beginning his coaching career at Texas A&M.

Kubiak will open the season against the Miami Dolphins and former Aggie star De'Von Achane, who is coming off a Pro Bowl season that helped him earn a new contract and become the centerpiece of Miami's offense. Kubiak will be without tight end Brock Bowers , but veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins and running back Ashton Jeanty should be available. Barring a last-minute trade, Maxx Crosby will anchor the Raiders' defense.

Gary Kubiak is a major reason the family name already carries weight in Aggieland. He played quarterback at Texas A&M from 1980–82 before returning as an assistant coach. His connection to the program helped introduce Aggie fans to Klint, who later began his coaching career at his father's alma mater.

Klint spent three seasons at Texas A&M, working under Mike Sherman in 2010 and 2011 before serving as a graduate assistant and working with the inside receivers under Kevin Sumlin in 2012. He also earned a master's degree in human resource development from Texas A&M.

Kubiak made the jump to the NFL as an assistant with the Minnesota Vikings in 2013. He bounced around to several teams before returning to Minnesota and eventually becoming the Vikings' offensive coordinator. He later spent time with San Francisco and New Orleans before taking over as the Seattle Seahawks ' offensive coordinator.

Kubiak helped lead Seattle to a 14-3 record while directing an offense that finished third in the NFL in scoring at 28.4 points per game. The season ended with the Seahawks winning Super Bowl LX and helped Kubiak earn his first opportunity to lead an NFL franchise.

Kubiak's time in Aggieland was only the beginning, but it gave him his first opportunity in coaching and added another chapter to his family's history with Texas A&M. Sixteen years later, the former Aggie assistant and graduate will begin the next stage of his career as an NFL head coach .

articles.body:
Editor's note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy!

The quarterback position will always rank near the top of the food chain, and with Washington , that certainly is the truth, as Jayden Daniels remains the player the Commanders can trust most to make the offense function. Head coach Dan Quinn has been beaming over Daniels since the microphone came on and he was asked a question post-draft about his command and accuracy. The biggest takeaway this year is that Daniels, while he didn't play much in the preseason, had more than 500 reps in camp , including two joint practice sessions (with Miami and Baltimore ). New offensive coordinator David Blough , while keeping the offense as secret as possible, has gone on and on about Daniels getting greater control of protections and operating from the huddle. While the room feels much deeper this season, Terry McLaurin is still the top receiver, although Stefon Diggs would make that argument interesting. Mix in rookie Antonio Williams and tight end Chig Okonkwo and the team should have multiple options for Daniels to excel with. What moves the ranking: Whether this ranking increases or decreases depends on several things this week against Philadelphia , including how Daniels plays in the new system, how well he does with more control and more time under center. Does he operate within the system, looking for the open man and getting rid of it when it's the best option, or does he try to play hero ball the second the play breaks down? He's ready to prove to the world that he's elite at the position, but there are a couple of last steps before he's there.

To read more of this article, CLICK HERE

the No. 2 overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft is gaining considerable hype regarding his bounce-back chances. And if Daniels returns to his old form, that could be a problem for the entire NFC East.

"Jayden Daniels can reclaim his place as a premier quarterback, and there's considerable hype in league circles that Daniels will get back on track and be a problem for the rest of the NFC East."

The NFL knows what Jayden Daniels can do, and he must remind them of that fact

It was a case of out of sight, out of mind for Daniels. This is a tale as old as time around the league. But if he gets a better run of luck on the health front, it would be surprising if he didn't have a major say in the season .

The athleticism, accuracy, poise, and intelligence are right where they need to be. Daniels is growing as a leader, with steely resolve and a natural aura that everyone seems to gravitate toward.

And in Blough's scheme, which should be better suited to his skills, a season more in keeping with his exceptional rookie exploits is well within Daniels' capabilities.

Everyone has to go through adversity at some stage. Daniels is no different, but last season's disaster has only made him stronger.

Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations

Faster commenting and posting experience!

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android .

Daronte Jones — Disguise can't become a liability

Question: "You spoke about wanting to kind of keep the offense on edge a little bit, making them react to you guys as a defense. How does disguising coverages and making it look like one thing before the snap when it's actually another thing after the snap help you guys toward that effort?"

"Yeah. Well, again, showing different looks is what we like to pride ourselves on, or try to anyway. But at the end of the day, we never want our disguise to become a liability. And so, you know, we don't want to be statues in terms of just standing still and trying to paint a different picture. So the more that we, as a defense, can handle that, then the more we can grow in that way. And so how much of that, or how little of that do we see, that's all depending on our personnel and how the guys feel comfortable. You know, the early part of the season, especially in a new scheme, guys want to just make sure, 'I'm where I need to be,' and that's totally all right as long as they're playing comfortable and fast."

With the group of guys they have assembled, it should be interesting to see the product on the field. If they can get turnovers, ther

David Blough — Antonio Williams is "made for big-time moments"

Question: "You have a rookie wide receiver making his NFL debut on Sunday, Antonio Williams. Curious in terms of what you've seen in his progression over this past month that makes you believe he's ready for this moment, and what type of factor can he be on Sunday?"

"Yeah, a lot of growth. I think since the first day we've had him, he has been a joy to work with, and you see kind of the eagerness to learn. And then as we've progressed throughout, him earning rep share, different things over the course of the time, he has not flinched in any moment. So, you know, similar to a lot of guys on our offense, he's made for kind of those big-time moments, and we knew that when we were evaluating him. He has confirmed that hunch since being here. So we're excited about him and his growth, and we'll see where it goes."

With the group they already have, if Williams can step forward and have a substantial season, the offense should really click in terms of moving the chains. It appears as if each receiver serves a different purpose, with a couple serving several.

Jones will run something similar to what he learned from Brian Flores with the Minnesota Vikings . That will mean a lot of sophisticated blitzing and disguised coverages.

So many moving parts will demand quick thinking and adjustments from Luvu. He'll be the voice of experience in the huddle, the player who rearranges alignments and switches in and out of play calls to keep the Commanders primed to execute Jones' mix of pressure and deception.

This new approach relies on creating confusion for offenses. It's a more thoughtful brand of defense than the reckless abandon Luvu often played with during his first two seasons as a member of the Commanders.

Getting everybody lined up, shifting would-be blitzing defenders in and out of gaps, and resetting coverage will test Luvu's mastery of the playbook. The Commanders are going to rely on the greater level of comfort Luvu has compared to top rookie Sonny Styles .

Commanders' new defense faces ideal first potential victim

The Eagles aren't short of talent offensively, but can they make their own new scheme work under first-year play-caller Sean Mannion? His biggest priority is getting quarterback Jalen Hurts back on track.

A useful runner, Hurts remains erratic as a passer . He lost marquee wide receiver A.J. Brown to a trade with the New England Patriots this offseason, and the Eagles now want Hurts to treat rookie Makai Lemon like an alpha target.

Hurts is the ideal first potential victim for the Commanders to confound with their multi-layered blitzing.

Styles was drafted seventh overall as the leader in the middle of the Commanders' defense. The former Ohio State Buckeye had a very successful college career that included a National Championship in 2024, and an All-American selection last year. Fans got a taste of what is to come in the preseason, but now the real games begin, and the expectations for Styles are very high. If his play comes close to his last season at Ohio State, he'll be in the running for Defensive Rookie of the Year. The transition from college to the pros is tough, though, and there's no telling whether or not a rookie can make the adjustments needed. How will he respond playing in his first NFL game in Philadelphia, where the fans will make themselves heard?

Both K'Lavon Chaisson (knee) and Odafe Oweh (calf) were limited during the practice week, so it's possible one of both of them could be on a pitch count. Both guys must perform well with the snaps available, especially with Dorance Armstrong serving a one game suspension.

Chaisson finished the 2025 season (with New England ) on absolute fire , showing an ability to get after and take down the quarterback. Operating at last year's level will put added pressure on Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and force game-changing mistakes, which Washington will need on Sunday, and Chaisson is the big-game player to provide them.

"Especially from the offensive side, we got a lot of young guys, but a lot of talent too. So, being that you have that fire and that passion, you know, it's being steered in the right direction. It's a little bit of accountability on both of us too, like, just as far as like, even just come down to walking off the field. We pride ourselves on not doing that and holding guys accountable and being open, catching the ball, being a receiver. But it's kind of being an engine of an offense, you know. You want to be the engine. You want to be one of the pieces of the engine at least, and you want to see that it goes well. So, it's fun to play with him. He's a hell of a talent. He's a hell of a guy. It's been a lot of fun. I look forward to it this season."

McLaurin and Diggs will be some of the top targets for Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels, who is looking to come back after his sophomore slump last year, which was severely affected by the various injuries he suffered. They will also be able to mentor rookie receiver Antonio Williams out of Clemson, whom Washington drafted in the third round of the NFL Draft.

SI Betting's Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week:

While I still believe the Eagles are the team to beat in the NFC East this season, there are still some things they have to prove to me before I'm ready to lay points on them. First of all, can they find a way to replace A.J. Brown's production at wide receiver with him now in New England? Also, I can't mention the Bears' record in one-score games without mentioning that the Eagles had an even better record in one-score games at 8-4.

Meanwhile, the Washington Commanders have filled some holes on their roster and are much healthier than they were a year ago. They need Jayden Daniels to get back to his 2024 form, but entering this season healthy should go a long way toward doing that.

I'm going to take the points with Washington.

I unfortunately agree with MacMillan here.

Philadelphia tends to make things harder than it needs to be, especially early in the season, and Washington is going to come out hungry after last year's divisional meetings.

Take a look behind the scenes as the Washington Commanders prepare for their season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles

WEEK ONE: Eagles Preview With HC Dan Quinn | Washington Commanders | The Gameplan | NFL

BTB: Do you think there will be a jump up from Jaxson Dart this season? Are you confident in his play?

BBV: I do think Dart will take a step forward. Winning and becoming the best player he can be means a lot to him. That should go without saying for professional athletes, but there are a lot of guys in pro sports who are just collecting paychecks. Dart is not one of them. Am I confident in his play? Yes, but he is a second-year QB making his first Week 1 start. There will be mistakes.

A year ago I believed that the Giants' roster was about to hit a critical mass of talent that would allow them to compete week in, week out, without needing to out-scheme their opponents or rely on lucky breaks to win. The results weren't there, but I do believe the overall talent on the roster put the Giants in position to win more often than not. What I didn't count on was a lack of accountability and attention to detail from the top down with the Giants' coaches.

This year, I believe the roster is stronger given the continued development of the 2024 and 2025 classes.

Ultimately, given all the unknowns in this game, I have to think it will come down to which squad is better prepared for Week 1. And while the Giants' veteran coaching staff is barely mentioned at the national level, I think they've been methodical in how they've approached the start of the season. I'm going to trust their experience and clear vision to have the team ready to go on Sunday night.

I have no doubts that this is going to be a tough, hard-fought match-up. But I'm going with the Giants starting the season with a statement.

On Sunday the Commanders backup offensive tackle will be either Esa Pole , who was signed to their practice squad after spending the preseason with the Chiefs; or Trent Scott , who the Commanders liked so much they cut him and signed DJ Humphries, who wasn't in anyone's training camp.

[ Note from Bill-in-Bangkok : Apparently unable to read a roster, BGN doesn't realize that Pole and Scott are both practice squad players, neither of whom was elevated for this game. The primary backup at offensive tackle will be 9-year veteran and 2-time super bowl champion, Andrew Wylie]

At cornerback, Rasul Douglas , who was available in July, will start in place of injured Trey Amos . These are pretty important positions to leave to freely available players as primary backups.

[Another note from Bill-in-Bangkok : While starters have not been announced by the team, reports from camp indicate that the starting CBs are likely to be Amik Robertson and Mikey Sainristil. Douglas and Moreau will be primary backups while Trey Amos is on IR. Meanwhile, the Eagles just put their rookie TE, drafted in the 2nd round on IR to avoid the indignity of making him inactive today per…let me see… per Bleeding Green Nation ]

The Adam Peters/Dan Quinn regime is 17-17, with a point differential of -1. If you want to include the playoffs, they're 19-18 with a point differential of -16.

What is it you say you do here Adam Peters?

Since taking over after the 2023 season, the offensive line, even when healthy, isn't significantly better [ BiB : ranked 13th in 2025 by PFF] . The running game still stinks [ BiB : 4th in the NFL in 2025 per ESPN] . The defense still can't stop the run, or the pass [ BiB : New coordinator; Oweh, Omenihu, Chaisson, Cross, Chenal, Settle, Styles added to defensive roster. We'll find out what they can stop this afternoon] . After having the oldest team in the league in 2025, they head into 2026 with the… 6th oldest team [ BiB : Yes, significantly younger and faster, but still with veteran leaders; two oldest players are the punter & long snapper – positions that everyone knows require youth & athleticism] . They have the 5th most salary cap space available [ BiB : 6th-most, but to know that, you have to be able to count] . Poor drafting, lousy free agent signings, and bad trades brought them right back to where they stared: their fourth double digit loss season in seven years [ BiB : reminder that not a single snap has yet been played this season outside of the addled brains of Eagles fans] .

If this was the state of the Eagles I'd be pissed.

To read more of this article [though I can't imagine why you would], CLICK HERE

The Eagles placing Stowers on IR means that the rookie tight end isn't eligible to return to the active roster until after Week 4. The remaining tight ends on the team: Dallas Goedert , Johnny Mundt , and E.J. Jenkins.

The timing of Stowers' new injury is a bit curious since he told reporters on Friday that he expected to play.

Even if Stowers was healthy enough to suit up, it was widely expected that he would be inactive for this game as the fourth tight end on the team's depth chart. The rookie struggled to make an impact on offense in training camp and preseason games … and he doesn't exactly offer a special teams background (six total ST snaps over five years of playing college football). By contrast, the Eagles have talked up Jenkins' ability to contribute in that phase of the game.

And so now Stowers will avoid being a healthy scratch, which wouldn't have been the most flattering look for him or the Eagles since he was a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

DeVonta Smith is WR1. That much is clear.

Dontayvion Wicks is WR2. Eagles wide receiver coach Aaron Moorehead left no ambiguity in declaring as much recently. And it tracks since Wicks was easily Hurts' top target when both DeVonta and Makai Lemon missed most of training camp due to hamstring injuries.

Who is WR3? The Eagles are listing Lemon as a starter on their team-issued depth chart . The 2026 first-round pick was taking all the first-team reps in the slot upon returning from injury in late August.

But it's fair to wonder if Lemon is currently ready to be the main man in that third receiver role. His preseason debut wasn't encouraging . I also didn't think Nick Sirianni gave him the strongest vote of confidence when asked about his role earlier this week:

The guess here is that Lemon will start but he'll share snaps with some combination of Elijah Moore , Hollywood Brown , and/or Darius Cooper . That would probably be for the best, since those players look more prepared to contribute to winning in Week 1.

The Commanders' path to victory probably looks something like this:

Jayden Daniels returns to 2024 form and totally balls out. He manages to run around and escape the Eagles' pass rush while having success throwing to their new top trio of Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs , and Chig Okonkwo. Maybe Riq Woolen 's volatility burns the Eagles' defense early on.

The Eagles' offense continues to look like a work in progress as the Commanders' new chaotic defense stifles that unit.

I do believe Daniels is the biggest reason why those doubting the Commanders could be wrong about them this week and their entire 2026 season outlook. I think it's possible…he finishes this year as the top quarterback in the NFC East.

For the Eagles, the microscopic coverage is the definition of a mixed blessing. On one hand, what organization or business wouldn't want such sustained attention? Can you imagine someone writing an article about your product every single day for seven consecutive years ? The financial value of the media exposure is incalculable — and one reason the Eagles are now worth $10.3 billion, the seventh-most valuable sports franchise in the world.

On the other hand, the year-round stream of articles, podcasts, and social posts has clearly contributed to what is now, at least in my opinion, an unhealthy mania around the Eagles — with every errant practice throw by the fourth-string quarterback setting off panic, and expectations for every season so high that nothing less than a Super Bowl victory will suffice. It's a mania, I should add, that's built to feed on itself: Fan interest leads to media scrutiny, which leads to deeper fan interest, which leads to even more scrutiny, which leads to even more obsessive fan interest, which leads to …

Take the case of Kevin Patullo, the assistant coach who last year was put in charge of the Eagles offense. When that unit, which was playing with significant injuries on the line, got off to a slow start, there were instant calls for Patullo to be fired. By November, the attitude about him had become so hostile that knuckleheads egged his house in South Jersey . The incident was covered by local TV, including 6ABC, which ended its report by interviewing an Eagles supporter outside a convenience store. The fan agreed that egging someone's house was over the line, though he added that Patullo stank at his job — and should be fired.

Can you imagine any other circumstance when a TV station would cover a crime — then let someone say the crime victim should lose his job?

Perhaps that's why the Eagles have grown more restrictive when it comes to player access. The chances of something innocuous being blown out of proportion are higher than ever. "They basically play defense now," one media member says of the team. "It's all about, how can this hurt us?"

articles.body:
Veteran edge-rusher Maxx Crosby was determined to remain with the Las Vegas Raiders after his trade to the Baltimore Ravens fell through, according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.

Rapoport reported Sunday the Los Angeles Rams made an effort to land Crosby as he was their "internal wish" before the Myles Garrett trade and "were the strongest club pushing for a deal."

"But before there could be anything official, Crosby let it be known to anyone interested that he did not want to be traded," per the report. "He wanted to remain with the Raiders, and he let his own organization know as well."

Rapoport, citing sources, also reported that Crosby has "had no issues and is said to be in excellent health."

articles.title: Washington Commanders vs. Philadelphia Eagles: NFL experts make Week 1 picks
articles.summary: Here's how the NFL experts are viewing the Week 1 matchup between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders open the 2026 season today at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia , where they'll face the two-time defending NFC East champion Eagles .

The Eagles head into Sunday's game as 5.5-point favorites , and that line has remained consistent throughout the week. Philadelphia will be without linebacker Jonathan Greenard , but is otherwise healthy. Every player on Washington's injury report will play on Sunday. The Commanders, of course, did lose left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps last month, meaning Brandon Coleman will start at left tackle. Coleman has started five games against the Eagles in his two NFL seasons.

Jayden Daniels is back under center for the Commanders after missing both meetings against the Eagles last season. Can Daniels lead Washington to a Week 1 upset?

We canvassed different NFL experts and the Eagles are an overwhelming pick.

All 11 of ESPN's experts picked Philadelphia, including Matt Bowen, Mike Clay and Jeremy Fowler.

The same goes for CBS ' panel of experts, although Dave Richard was the only one of seven analysts to pick the Commanders.

NFL Pickwatch , which collects expert picks from almost every outlet, has a whopping 98% of picks made in favor of Philadelphia. Back in 2022, the Eagles were undefeated and faced the Commanders. Philly was at home, and 99% of the experts picked the Eagles. Guess who won that one?

Don't count out the Commanders. Anything can happen in the NFL, especially in Week 1.

articles.title: New Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors Leak As Star CB Out for Steelers amid Injury Concern
articles.summary: A trade involving Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. "is very possible," according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
A trade involving Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. "is very possible," according to Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.

As a result of a back injury, Porter was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

The 26-year-old's desire for a new contract is a major storyline as well. Per Schefter and Rapoport, he's "open to playing elsewhere," but a trade is far from close to materializing.

"The Steelers have been open to listening to offers for Porter, sources say," they wrote. "But there has not been notable interest at Pittsburgh's asking price of a premium draft pick — possibly in the first round — and no serious trade talks have developed despite the Steelers' willingness to deal him."

Porter is in the final year of his rookie contract and will get a nice pay bump whenever he signs his next deal. He has a $3.9 base salary for 2026, and Spotrac set his market value at $23.4 million.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported in August that Porter "has not been happy with the way things have gone." One point of frustration is that Pittsburgh committed financially to others on the roster without making what he deemed to be a serious offer.

Days ago, Porter told reporters he's not attempting to reset the cornerback market.

An extension could push him into the $30 million range , though. Six corners are in that group, and two (New England Patriots' Christian Gonzalez and Seattle Seahawks' Devon Witherspoon) penned new contracts that average more than $33 million annually.

Rapoport and Schefter noted the Steelers don't negotiate extensions once the season kicks off, so the window has seemingly closed for them to make a breakthrough with Porter's representatives.

Once he's cleared from the back injury, Porter won't have much recourse but to play, either. A regular-season holdout would be far too costly in terms of lost earnings and missed game time.

A trade would potentially suit both parties, but Sunday's report painted a clear picture of how little traction that market has right now.
