articles.title: De'Zhaun Stribling Injury Update, Surgery Plan and Timeline for Return Revealed in New 49ers Rumors
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will reportedly be without promising rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling for at least a month.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers will reportedly be without promising rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling for at least a month.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Stribling suffered a deltoid sprain in his ankle during Thursday's season-opening win over the Los Angeles Rams.

"Stribling is still seeking opinions, and while surgery is not currently planned, it is possible," Rapoport added while noting he is expected to miss at least a month of action. "SF will be cautious."

This is quite the blow for a 49ers team that will already be without fellow wide receiver Ricky Pearsall for the season due to a PCL injury that required surgery.

They have veterans Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel, as well as tight end George Kittle, to lead the way in the aerial attack, but Stribling was expected to play a major role as another option for quarterback Brock Purdy with Pearsall sidelined.

San Francisco selected the Ole Miss product with a second-round pick in this year's draft, and it didn't take long for him to receive plenty of hype in fantasy football circles.

Stribling helped lead Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals last season with 55 catches for 811 yards and six touchdowns before he stood out leading up to the NFL draft because of his combination of size and speed.

Given the defensive attention Evans, Samuel and Kittle typically draw when they are on the field, the rookie figured to be an immediate contributor who could take advantage of space, favorable matchups and single coverage.

However, that will have to wait following his setback.

The 49ers return home for the next three games against the Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals and Denver Broncos before a Week 5 showdown on the road against the division-rival Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 11.

That would be approximately one month after the Sept. 10 opener in which Stribling suffered the injury, although the team is understandably using caution with more of a long-term approach with the rookie.

articles.title: Human vs ChatGPT in NFL Week 1 betting picks, from Bears and Packers to Texans and Lions
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears, Green Bay Packers and Washington Commanders headline a human-vs.-ChatGPT NFL betting showdown with 10 total Week 1 picks.
articles.body: I’m not sure why I keep doing this to myself, but I’ve decided to spend the NFL season going head-to-head with ChatGPT in a battle of betting picks. Each week, I’ll make my five best NFL bets. Then ChatGPT will make its five best bets from the same odds board. We’ll track both records throughout the season and let the results determine who actually knows what they're talking about. 2026 NFL SEASON PREDICTIONS: DIVISION WINNERS, PLAYOFF TEAMS AND SUPER BOWL PICK REVEALED I expect ChatGPT to wipe the floor with me. It has access to more information than any human could process, while I have a long and proud history of giving people reasons to bet against me. If it can’t beat me, all those people predicting AI will take over the world are clearly wrong. The lines used will be the best available numbers when the picks are made. I reserve the right to complain that I was on the right side and just got unlucky, but the record will count the same either way. If ChatGPT gets one wrong, however, it wasn’t unlucky. It was just wrong. No moving the goalposts for the robot. First up: my five picks. Then, ChatGPT’s five picks. Dan's Card 1. Chicago Bears -3 (-106) Chicago Bears at Carolina Panthers, 1 p.m. ET (FOX) Dan's analysis: I don't love laying three on the road in Week 1 but the Bears are a team on the rise that came within a play of reaching the NFC Championship last year. The Panthers made the playoffs, but they weren't all that good and are due for negative regression. GPT’s analysis: Solid price on the better team, and Chicago’s offense should match up well with Carolina’s zone-heavy defense. The concern is laying a full field goal on the road with several Bears carrying injury questions. 2. Browns–Jaguars Under 40½ (-110) Cleveland Browns at Jacksonville Jaguars, 1 p.m. ET (CBS) Dan's analysis: Simple: where are the points going to come from? Deshaun Watson and the Browns? Well, maybe, but only if it's Watson throwing pick-6s or turning the ball over deep in his own territory. I also like getting a few unders on the card because Week 1 unders are 52-28 (65%) over the past five seasons, including a 12-4 mark last year. GPT’s analysis: Cleveland’s quarterback and offensive-line uncertainty create a very low scoring floor; the danger is Jacksonville or its defense producing most of the points. 3. Washington Commanders +5½ (-106) Washington Commanders at Philadelphia Eagles, 4:25 p.m. ET (FOX) Dan's analysis: I'm expecting a big bounce-back from Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders this season and I think it starts in Week 1. The addition of Stefon Diggs gives the team another weapon and it's going to matter against Philadelphia. The Eagles, conversely, seem primed for a step back and I'm concerned about Jalen Hurts leaning on DeVonta Smith as his No. 1 receiver. CONTROVERSIAL PREDICTIONS AND RANKINGS OF ALL 32 NFL STARTING QBS JUST IN TIME FOR REGULAR-SEASON KICKOFF GPT’s analysis: This is the pick I like least. ESPN’s FPI still favors Philadelphia by 4.8 points, which creates only a thin numerical edge on Washington +5½, but its weakened offensive line against Philadelphia’s defensive front could overwhelm that advantage. 4. Dolphins–Raiders Under 41 (-110) Miami Dolphins at Las Vegas Raiders, 4:25 p.m. ET (FOX) Dan's analysis: I don't have a lot to say here because it's roughly the same as the Browns-Jaguars analysis. I don't see either team scoring much, especially with Malik Willis and Kirk Cousins guiding these two offenses. GPT’s analysis: Strong pick—Brock Bowers’ absence and Miami’s unsettled offense give both teams low scoring floors. 5. Green Bay Packers ML (+110) Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS) Dan's analysis: I almost feel like a sucker taking this bet because it feels like the most obvious play on the card. But how can I not jump on the better team as an underdog against a team starting another new quarterback this season? I think Kevin O'Connell is an excellent coach and Kyler Murray will thrive under him, but I think it will take a few weeks to come together. GPT’s analysis: Packers moneyline is my favorite pick on your card and our only overlap. ESPN’s FPI favors Green Bay outright, although the absences of Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs make it far from comfortable. GPT's Card For full transparency, I used GPT-5.6 Sol Max mode, fed it the OddsChecker board as it appeared Saturday at 6 p.m. ET and gave it the following prompt: "I’m writing an article in which I go head-to-head with you, ChatGPT, on NFL bets. Here’s how it will work: Pick your five best bets for Sunday based on the odds provided. No bet can be priced worse than -120. Review every spread, total and moneyline that falls within those parameters and determine whether it belongs among your five picks. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you're passing on the eligible bets you don't select." THESCORE BET PROMO CODE: GET A $1000 BET RESET AHEAD OF THE OPENING NFL SUNDAY OF THE 2026 SEASON GPT took nearly 20 minutes to produce these five picks: 1. Houston Texans +1½ (-108) Buffalo Bills at Houston Texans, 1 p.m. ET (CBS) GPT’s analysis: Houston’s defense is healthy and has repeatedly troubled Josh Allen. ESPN’s FPI projects Buffalo by only one point—still a Houston cover—while most ESPN and NFL.com panelists picked Houston outright. I prefer the points over Houston’s moneyline at +105 because a one-point Buffalo win cashes the spread. Projection: Houston 21, Buffalo 20 Dan's analysis: I hate this pick. Sorry, but I just can't bet against Josh Allen and the Bills, especially in Week 1. Houston won nine straight games to end the 2025 regular season, but they mostly beat up on bad teams and, yes, they beat the Bills but it was a home game on a short week. Even their playoff win was against a mediocre Pittsburgh team. 2. Buccaneers–Bengals Under 50½ (-108) Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Cincinnati Bengals, 1 p.m. ET (FOX) GPT’s analysis: Fifty-one points is a demanding Week 1 threshold. Both defenses added personnel, both starting quarterbacks barely played during the preseason and Tampa Bay’s receiving depth is compromised. ESPN analyst Ben Solak recommended the same under at the worse price of -112. Projection: Cincinnati 26, Tampa Bay 23 Dan's analysis: I don't hate this look at all. As mentioned, unders are typically hot in Week 1 and this game screams OVER given the two offenses. Usually when a pick seems obvious, take the other side. In this case, that's the under. Good pick, GPT. 3. Detroit Lions -7 (-106) New Orleans Saints at Detroit Lions, 1 p.m. ET (FOX) GPT’s analysis: Detroit averaged 28.3 points last season and has recently been the league’s most productive home offense. New Orleans brings weak pass protection, has ruled out Cameron Jordan and lists Alvin Kamara as questionable. Exactly seven pushes, so I would not play -7½. Projection: Detroit 31, New Orleans 20 Dan's analysis: Well, this is the other side of the obvious coin. I feel like the public is going to hammer Detroit. I wouldn't be confident betting against the Lions, but I don't love laying the seven, either. I'd avoid this one, personally. 4. Los Angeles Chargers -9 (-110) Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Chargers, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS) GPT’s analysis: ESPN’s FPI projects a 9.6-point margin, and four of NFL.com’s five projected scores cover -9. Arizona allowed 35.2 points per game over its final nine games last season and now has two secondary starters out. Projection: Chargers 30, Arizona 17 Dan's analysis: Again, I just hate laying these huge numbers in Week 1. The public loves big favorites and we just don't know enough about these teams to lay more than a touchdown. This is an avoid for me. 5. Green Bay Packers ML (+110) Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS) GPT’s analysis: ESPN’s FPI gives Green Bay a 56.8% win probability, while +110 requires only a 47.6% win probability. Jordan Love finished 2025 third in Total QBR. The moneyline also strictly improves upon Green Bay -½ at +106: It pays more and pushes on a tie. Projection: Green Bay 24, Minnesota 23 Dan's analysis: Well, since I also made this bet, I'm obviously a fan. Great job, GPT. Or, more likely, terrible job since my picks are notoriously bad. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But we’ll see. Check back next week to see how we both did. articles.title: Sam Darnold 'Hurt His Butt,' Rapoport Says as New Injury Update Revealed in Seahawks Rumors
articles.summary: While Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold may be sidelined for the immediate future, he reportedly avoided a significant, season-ending injury during Wednesday's season-opening win over the New England Patriots.
articles.body:
While Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold may be sidelined for the immediate future, he reportedly avoided a significant, season-ending injury during Wednesday's season-opening win over the New England Patriots.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Darnold will miss "probably a couple games" before adding, "they've been calling it a hip injury. My understanding is that it's actually a glute injury. So Darnold hurt his butt. It's a muscular injury not considered to be major."

Seattle doesn't want to be without its starting quarterback for any time, but there is surely an element of relief with this diagnosis.

Darnold exiting Wednesday's win over the Patriots with the injury he suffered on the team's opening possession overshadowed much of the game, at least from the Seahawks' perspective. Yet it seems like he will be back sooner rather than later, even if that means missing the next two games at the Arizona Cardinals and at the Washington Commanders.

The Seahawks showed the formula for treading water without Darnold as well against the Patriots.

Backup Drew Lock entered the game in the starter's absence and got the ball into his top playmaker's hands with the game on the line. He found Jaxon Smith-Njigba with a short pass on a fourth-down attempt in the fourth quarter, and the reigning Offensive Player of the Year did the rest of the work from there and burst past the defense for a touchdown.

Seattle also relied on its stout defense and picked off Drake Maye three times, including one from Josh Jobe in the end zone in the final seconds to clinch the win.

As long as Lock can manage the game by getting it to JSN and others while the defense continues to play at a high level, the reigning Super Bowl champions should be able to handle a short-term absence from Darnold.

And that will put them in an ideal position to challenge for another deep playoff run once he does return to the lineup.

articles.title: Demarcus Robinson, Top Fantasy Waiver-Wire WRs as De'Zhaun Stribling Injury Revealed in 49ers Rumors
articles.summary: Any fantasy football managers with De'Zhaun Stribling on their roster will need to look in a different direction for the next few weeks.
articles.body:
Any fantasy football managers with De'Zhaun Stribling on their roster will need to look in a different direction for the next few weeks.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reported the rookie wide receiver is sidelined for at least a month with a deltoid sprain in his ankle.

That's going to put a bigger spotlight on Demarcus Robinson, who had two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown in San Francisco's 27-7 Week 1 win over the Los Angeles Rams.

If Deebo Samuel Sr. happens to be available in your league, then he's a must-add as well.

Outside of San Francisco, the Philadelphia Eagles' Dontayvion Wicks and New York Giants' Malachi Fields could be worth a look depending on how Week 1 unfolds.

As a flex option, Kaelon Black's value is ticking up even higher. The Niners running back ran for 65 yards on 14 carries against Los Angeles, so he might get enough touches, even as the backup to Christian McCaffrey, to make a fantasy impact.

In general, there's no need to move right now. Players on the 49ers roster are ineligible to add until Week 1 concludes, and the opening slate of games will provide a better picture of the overlooked candidates who are worthy of a waiver claim.

Fields, for example, generated some excitement during training camp and the preseason. If he's totally anonymous Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys, the hype is going to quiet down.

Fantasy managers who have IR spots available to use may not want to cut ties with Stribling just yet. There's nothing to lose by stashing him away.

Those who don't have that luxury should start looking at the waiver wire as soon as the window opens in Week 2. A month is a long time for Stribling to miss and the payoff at the end once he's cleared may not be worth it.

articles.summary: Scott Hanson confirms 'RedZone' will air limited 15-second commercials between plays this season, but promises fewer ads than last year's count
articles.body: The NFL's popular "RedZone" broadcast returns for its 18th season on Sunday, and while the focus is seemingly on how many commercials the previously commercial-free program will air, host Scott Hanson has other things up his sleeve. But first, the commercials thing: "There will be, there will be what people define as commercials," Hanson told OutKick recently. "The plan is right now to have a limited number of 15-second commercials only in between plays. 'NFL REDZONE' HOST SCOTT HANSON SAYS HE UNDERSTANDS FAN FRUSTRATION OVER COSTLY STREAMING SUBSCRIPTIONS "So we're on a Dallas Cowboys drive. OK, first-and-10 after a 5-yard gain. They're walking back to the huddle. That's when we will splice in one standalone, 15-second commercial. I can confirm that for you." "RedZone" aired 16 advertisements of some kind at one point last season, which marked a significant increase for what was once seven hours of commercial-free programming. Hanson said fears that the number will increase to start the 2026 season are unfounded. In fact, there will be fewer at the start of the season. That, of course, says nothing about what will happen later this season, but Hanson isn’t making those decisions. "The rest of it is up to the business folks and Uncle Scott doesn't make the decisions when it comes to the business folks at the NFL," he said. "But yes, there will be advertisements, a limited number, what I would describe as a limited amount, but fans can make their own minds up about that." Fans made up their minds about "RedZone" and Hanson a long time ago, and those fans have come from some unlikely places. "I've been told we've been on in the White House in the last two administrations, so both sides of the aisle," Hanson said. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS "I've been told by the players ... Tom Brady, loves ‘RedZone,’ loved it when he was a player, when he was playing on Monday Night Football or Thursday night football or the bye week, he was watching ‘RedZone.’ "Josh Allen — one of the faces of the NFL today — loves ‘RedZone.’ When he's playing on an off day or whatever, if he can watch ‘RedZone.’ So it's just, it's, it's a phenomenon." Hanson, back with Lowe's for the second year of the popular "Earn Your Sunday" campaign along with Dak Prescott, Christian McCaffrey and Justin Jefferson, is something of a renaissance man. He's visited six of the planet's seven continents and promises to eventually make it to Antarctica, the only continent he's missed. Hanson has cage dived with great white sharks and found himself at somewhat safe distances from lions on the Serengeti. He's also visited the Great Wall of China. All that begs some rapid fire questions: So, what's his adventure vacation preference, running with the bulls in Pamplona or climbing Mount Kilimanjaro? "I've done both," Hanson said. "Kilimanjaro was more beautiful. Running with the bulls required more courage. Running with the bulls." More afraid of great white sharks or lions? "Lions, because you don't have bars in front of you when you go on safari in the Serengeti plain," Hanson said. "I had bars in front of me when the great whites came up." Because he visited both China and Mexico, we have to ask: Mexican or Chinese food? OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "Oh, Mexican," Hanson said. "Only because in China, the Chinese food is not like American Chinese food. Let me just tell you that I ate a thing called duck dong. And I'm like, what is duck dong? I like it, it's real tasty, until they slowed down, and I learned they were speaking English, and they were saying duck tongue. "Duck tongue is what they were feeding me. Yeah, no. Give me Mexican." Seven hours of RedZone begins at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Travis Hunter's WR Role Revealed in New NFL Rumors Before Jaguars' Game vs. Browns
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars reportedly plan on using two-way playmaker Travis Hunter primarily as a cornerback during Sunday's season-opening game against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars reportedly plan on using two-way playmaker Travis Hunter primarily as a cornerback during Sunday's season-opening game against the Cleveland Browns.

"Travis Hunter, my understanding, is going to be a full-time cornerback," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported. "Not the full-time receiver that he was last year. He's still going to play receiver, he's got some packages. It's not red zone. I wondered if it might be.

"It's not, it's more of a speciality situation. Basically, whenever they need him. That is the plan for this week, full-time corner and part-time receiver. It could actually flip next week or in the following weeks because he is that talented."

As Rapoport mentioned, this is a switch from Hunter's rookie season.

According to Pro Football Reference , he was on the field for 324 offensive snaps and 162 defensive snaps in 2025 before he suffered a torn LCL that limited him to seven games.

Hunter tallied 28 catches for 298 yards and one touchdown as a wide receiver to go with 15 tackles, three passes defended and one fumble recovery as a cornerback. His ability to impact the game in multiple ways surely played a role in Jacksonville's decision to trade up and select him with the No. 2 overall pick of the 2025 NFL draft, and he showed flashes of that ability before the injury.

Yet Jacksonville has plenty of firepower in the aerial attack heading into the 2026 season.

Trevor Lawrence can target Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers and Brenton Strange, which gives him matchups to exploit all over the field. While Hunter would add another wrinkle with his speed, the Jaguars have more than enough weapons to thrive without him.

That makes him more important as a cornerback, and he will reportedly primarily focus on that in the opener.

Still, it is a testament to his overall talent that Rapoport suggested the roles could be flipped in the future depending on matchups. If nothing else, that will keep opponents guessing as the Jaguars look to get the most out of their second-year playmaker.

articles.title: Myles Garrett to Undergo Surgery, Latest NFL Rumors on Injury Timeline for Return to Rams
articles.summary: After a disappointing debut with the Los Angeles Rams in Thursday's loss against the San Francisco 49ers, reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is set to be sidelined for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
After a disappointing debut with the Los Angeles Rams in Thursday's loss against the San Francisco 49ers, reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett is set to be sidelined for the foreseeable future.

According to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Garrett is set to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and will be placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the next four weeks. Garrett will miss games against the New York Giants, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills. His next chance to return to the field will be when the Rams host the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6.

Garrett failed to record a single tackle in Los Angeles' 27-7 loss to San Francisco in the NFL Melbourne Game.

Per ESPN's Sarah Barshop , the star edge rusher called his performance "the worst version of myself that I've put out there" and revealed that his knee wasn't 100 percent healthy entering the game. He had sat out most of training camp while dealing with what Rams coach Sean McVay described as swelling in his knee.

"When I was out there, I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed," Garrett said after the loss. "I wasn't who I needed to be for my team."

The Rams acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in the biggest blockbuster trade of the offseason. He earned his second career DPOY award in 2025 after setting a new single-season sack record with 23. His arrival to Los Angeles made the team the clear-cut Super Bowl favorite and also convinced three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald to end his retirement and pursue another championship ring.

For now, the Rams will have to forge ahead without their prized offseason acquisition. They will certainly be hoping to have Garrett back at full strength as the playoffs approach.

Ahead of his first career NFL game, Cincinnati Bengals rookie defensive tackle Landon Robinson made the most of his pregame arrival.

Robinson wore his Navy service uniform to Cincinnati's Paycor Stadium for Sunday's season opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers:

The Bengals announced that Robinson will be among the inactive players for Sunday's Week 1 matchup.

A seventh-round pick in this year's draft, Robinson played three seasons at Navy, totaling 153 tackles and 14.5 sacks. He finished the 2025 season with career highs of 64 tackles and 6.5 sacks on his way to earning American Conference Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-American honors.

After missing the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, the Bengals are hoping to return to title contention this season. The team has long been known for its high-powered offense, but it bolstered its defense this offseason by signing defensive end Boye Mafe and safety Bryan Cook in free agency and trading for Pro Bowl defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II. Star quarterback Joe Burrow boldly declared that he's looking to lead Cincinnati to a Super Bowl title.

The Bengals will get started with their title chase on Sunday in a tough test against a motivated Bucs team.

articles.title: Rams reportedly tried to trade for Maxx Crosby after Ravens' deal fell through
articles.summary: Maxx Crosby reportedly told teams he did not want to be traded.
articles.body:
In another timeline, Maxx Crosby and not Myles Garrett , would have already played in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. Following his failed trade to the Baltimore Ravens , Crosby was reportedly pursued by a number of teams, including the Los Angeles Rams , according to ESPN.

That deal — and offers from other teams — never materialized, leading to Crosby staying with the Las Vegas Raiders to start the 2026 season. Of all the subsequent offers for Crosby, the Rams' deal came the closest to getting done, per ESPN.

It was a tumultuous offseason for Crosby, who in March was traded to the Ravens in exchange for multiple first-round picks. Days later, however, the Ravens backed out of the deal due to a failed physical by Crosby, who had surgery on his knee in the offseason.

If Crosby was upset about the deal falling through, he didn't show it. Shortly after the news, Crosby tweeted, " I'm a Raider. I'm back. " That tweet also seemed to imply Crosby did not want to be traded away once the Ravens' deal fell apart.

But that didn't stop other teams from trying, per ESPN. The Rams, Dallas Cowboys , Philadelphia Eagles and San Francsico 49ers were reportedly all involved in potential offers for Crosby, many of which were for "pennies on the dollars," according to ESPN.

Crosby, meanwhile, reportedly kept telling teams he wanted to remain with the Raiders.

With the Rams and Raiders failing to come together on a trade, Los Angeles eventually opted to go all-in for Myles Garrett. The move cost the team Jared Verse and multiple draft picks .

Since entering the NFL in 2019, Crosby has emerged as one of the best defensive ends in football. The 29-year-old has made five straight Pro Bowls and has led the league in tackles for loss twice.

In 2025, the Raiders signed Crosby to a three-year, $106.5 million extension , keeping him in Las Vegas through the 2029 NFL season.
